purpose: Defects found by the implementing agent rather than raised by an independent reviewer. Alex Zamurko, 5 October 2026: 'do not fabricate reviewer provenance, but do not leave a known defect outside controlled state tracking either.'
not_the_ledger: Entries here are never written into a review ledger and carry no cycle-generated identifier. A ledger finding is a finding a reviewer raised against a reviewed target, and its identifier encodes the cycle that raised it; inventing one for a defect no cycle produced would forge the provenance the ledger exists to establish.

states.REPAIRED_UNREVIEWED: a repair has landed with controls behind it, and nobody independent has examined it
states.REVIEWER_CONFIRMED: an independent review examined the entry and agreed it was a defect
states.RESOLVED: an independent review examined the repair in a later target and found it held

obligation: Every entry not in RESOLVED must be put to the next independent review explicitly, and must appear in any approval package built while it is in that state.

SELF-F01.description: The approval package could present a run with frozen review cycles and no ledger as a document with empty findings headings. A reader skimming it would see no findings, when the true state was that no reviewer had reported. Absence of evidence became evidence of absence.
SELF-F01.discovery_source: Implementer-disclosed. The suite test_approval_package.py was red from 1 October 2026 and was declared as a known-red control suite in every freeze of BOOTSTRAP-002. Alex Zamurko named the underlying behaviour as a control defect rather than a failing test on 5 October 2026.
SELF-F01.affected_component: scripts/approval_package.py, with its controls in scripts/test_approval_package.py. Neither is a covered component and nothing covered imports them, so this defect is outside the BOOTSTRAP-002 review target.
SELF-F01.severity: High for an approval decision, low for the running system. It cannot corrupt a record or a cycle; it can mislead the person deciding, which is the one reader the package exists for. BOOTSTRAP-003's reviewer refused the broader claim this register made, that none of these defects can produce a false green: this one can still present an empty findings category as a finished one.
SELF-F01.proposed_repair: Third repair, and the only one still standing; the first two are below in the history, each rejected by an independent reviewer. The package no longer decides any finding's state. The controller gained a --json flag that prints the governing boundary and the §6 sets from the boundary walk it already performs, and the package reads those instead of the `state` field cached in the ledger; if the controller cannot establish a state, the package refuses with FINDINGS_STATE: CANNOT_ESTABLISH rather than printing a category. A flag rather than a second walk inside the package, because §6's exit order is load-bearing and a copy of it would be free to disagree. The two earlier repairs are kept rather than removed: requiring the ledger to be readable, and reconciling what each frozen cycle reported against it, are still necessary, and were simply never sufficient.
evidence: scripts/loop_state.py: the --json branch, printing the walk's own `cur` at the governing boundary
scripts/approval_package.py: FINDINGS_STATE: CANNOT_ESTABLISH on a non-zero or unparseable controller result, and the categories built from the controller's open/resolved/disputed

scripts/test_approval_package.py: the reviewer's own fixture, 'an invalidated demonstration is reported as unresolved, not from the ledger's cached RESOLVED', with its baseline 'a demonstrated repair is reported as resolved', so a package that called everything unresolved could not satisfy both
The earlier repairs' controls are retained: the missing, unreadable and readable-but-empty ledger cases

history.note: Named as a functional control defect in workflow: 'absence of evidence must not become evidence of absence', and ruled that it be tracked in a register of its own rather than written into the reviewer ledger.
Repair landed with three controls. Unreviewed: no independent reviewer has looked at it, so the state says so rather than claiming the matter closed.

Closure not supported. The repair handled the two ways a ledger can fail to be READ, missing and unparseable, and not the way it can fail to be TRUE: a readable ledger holding {"findings": {}} beside a valid review reporting a finding still produced a package with exit 0, saying None under unresolved findings and marking the coverage item present. Reproduced by the reviewer.

Second repair: the findings each frozen cycle reported are reconciled against the ledger before any category is asserted empty, read through loop_state's own reader rather than a second one written in the package generator. A disagreement is CANNOT_ESTABLISH. Controlled by a fixture whose ledger is valid and parses and simply holds none of what the cycle beside it reported.

Closure still unsupported, second time. The membership check fixed the readable-but-empty ledger, and the package then grouped findings by the `state` field cached in the ledger rather than by the state the controller reconstructs. In an isolated fixture the reviewer invalidated the cycle containing a demonstration while retaining its cached RESOLVED: the controller reconstructed the finding as OPEN and reported CONTINUE, and the package exited 0, printed None under unresolved findings and counted one resolved. Required: generate the categories from the governing projected state, or refuse when that state cannot be established.

Third repair. The controller gained a --json flag that prints the governing boundary and its sets from the walk it already performs, and the package reads that instead of the cached fields; if the controller cannot establish a state, the package refuses with CANNOT_ESTABLISH. A flag rather than a second boundary walk in the package: the exit order is load-bearing and a copy of it would be free to disagree. Two controls, the reviewer's own fixture and its baseline, because a package that called everything unresolved would satisfy the first alone. Both of my first attempts at those controls passed by matching the full-ledger dump at the foot of the document rather than the section they named, which is the same defect in the control as in the tool.

Third repair supported, at the third attempt. The reviewer: 'The package obtains the controller's governing-boundary sets instead of grouping cached ledger states, and refuses an unsuccessful or unreadable controller result. The preserved run records both the resolved baseline and invalidated-demonstration control passing.' Three limits are the reviewer's own and are recorded rather than smoothed over. First, they could not execute the controls: 'the available Python commands failed to launch, and WSL access was denied', so the controls were read in source and in the preserved run output, not run. Second, only half the repair sits in the reviewed target: loop_state.py is a covered component and carries the --json branch, while approval_package.py is not covered and was seen as auxiliary evidence. Third, the same review raised a defect in the half that is covered, the --json interface returning prose with exit 0 when every cycle is invalid, which is SELF-F04 below. RESOLVED here means what this register says it means, that an independent review examined the repair in a later target and found it held, and nothing more.

SELF-F02.description: The mutation probe writes a deliberately broken line into tracked source, runs a suite, and restores the file in a finally block. A finally does not run when the process is killed outright, which is what closing a terminal window does. A killed run therefore left a disabled check sitting in the repository, with every suite passing for a reason other than the one it names, and nothing else in the repository able to notice.
SELF-F02.discovery_source: Implementer-disclosed. The probe's own docstring has named this risk since late September, and the mitigation was a start-time guard that only catches it on the next run. It happened on 5 October 2026: a PowerShell window was closed mid-run and left 'if False:' in scripts/loop_state.py, where it sat until the next probe run refused to start.
SELF-F02.affected_component: _probe/mutate_repairs.py. Not a covered component; it is preserved in cycle evidence as an instrument, and the review of 4 October states explicitly that its results are assertions rather than executed evidence.
SELF-F02.severity: Moderate. It cannot alter a record or a frozen cycle. It can make every suite in the repository pass while a check is switched off, and a commit made in that window would carry the disabled check into the history. The window on 5 October was about forty minutes and nothing was committed in it.
SELF-F02.proposed_repair: Record the mutation on disk before the file is touched, carrying the finding, the path, HEAD, and the digest of the text about to be written. The next run restores from HEAD and says what it did. The recovery is narrow on purpose: if HEAD has moved or the file is not byte for byte what the probe wrote, it refuses and says so rather than overwriting an edit made since.
evidence: _probe/mutate_repairs.py: ACTIVE, recover(), the record written before the mutation and removed in the same finally as the restore

Demonstrated on 5 October 2026 by killing a run with Stop-Process -Force, which does not unwind: the sentinel named scripts/cycle_projection.py, and the next run restored it from HEAD, reported the recovery, and then ran clean
.gitignore: the record is untracked, because a commit is never mid-mutation

history.note: Observed directly: a closed window left a mutation applied, and the clean-tree guard reported it one run later.
Repair landed and was demonstrated by reproducing the kill rather than by simulating it. Unreviewed, like SELF-F01.

Repair not demonstrated as claimed. Recovery ran `git checkout -- <path>`, which restores from the INDEX, while the message said HEAD. In a fixture with unchanged HEAD, mutated working bytes and different staged bytes, it returned 0, wrote the staged bytes, deleted the sentinel and reported restoration from HEAD. The claim in the output was false and nothing in the repository could have noticed.

Second repair: the bytes are read with `git show HEAD:<path>`, which names its source in the command, cannot be satisfied from the index, and leaves the index untouched because someone else's staged work is not this probe's to revert. The restored file is then verified against HEAD's bytes rather than the command's exit code being trusted. Controlled for the first time: scripts/test_probe_recovery.py, five controls including the reviewer's own staged-bytes fixture. Writing those controls found a second defect he had not reported, that recovery ran AFTER the argument filter, so a run whose filter matched nothing exited with the mutation still applied; recovery now runs before anything else.

Looked at and not confirmed. The reviewer: 'No new contrary evidence established here. Their prior assessments retain their stated limits; this review adds no fresh execution verification.' The state does not move. A review that found nothing against a repair is not a review that found the repair holds, and the second repair has still never been examined by anyone independent. Recorded so the next reader can see that cycle 03 looked rather than assuming it did not.

SELF-F03.description: The §15 gold runner scored the candidate and the baseline by two different rules. A candidate work may match a gold item under any phrasing the manuscript used for it, and that remapping ran over the candidate only; the baseline, loaded later in the same function, never received it. Every before-and-after comparison therefore gave the candidate matches the baseline was denied, which inflates the apparent improvement by however many works the manuscript phrases two ways. The same block also popped a key that already matched gold, so a work already counted correct could be moved off its match and reported as a regression that never happened.
SELF-F03.discovery_source: Implementer-disclosed, 6 October 2026, and found by accident rather than by looking. The record-level diff of two extractor runs over gold paper 1 showed the outputs byte-identical, and the gold runner then scored them 93/98 and 96/98 with one regression. Two identical files cannot differ, so one of the two measurements had to be wrong. Running the same candidate file as both candidate and baseline reproduced it in one command.
SELF-F03.affected_component: scripts/gold_runner.py, with its controls in scripts/test_gold_runner.py. Not a covered component of BOOTSTRAP-002; it belongs to the citation product rather than to the review layer.
SELF-F03.severity: High for anything measured. It does not corrupt a record or a cycle, and it cannot produce a false green in the review layer. What it does is make every improvement figure quoted through --baseline too favourable, including the +0.011 and +0.040 recorded in citation_extract.py for rc3 B1a, and the figure measured for this very ruling today, which fell from +4 to +3 once the scorer was fixed. Any decision taken on one of those numbers was taken on a number that flattered the change.
SELF-F03.proposed_repair: Lift the remapping into a function and apply it to both sides, so the two extractors are compared by one rule rather than the rule being compared with itself. Never move a key that already matches gold. Control it by scoring one candidate against itself: it must report zero regressions and one total, and the fixture must carry a variant or the control passes on the broken code too.
evidence: scripts/gold_runner.py: apply_variants(), called for the candidate and for the baseline, with the `ck in G` guard
scripts/test_gold_runner.py: 'a candidate compared with itself: no regressions, one total'
Before the fix, one file against itself: baseline 93/98, candidate 96/98, 1 regression, exit 3. After: 96/98 both sides, 0 regressions, exit 0
The re-measure of the 6 October grammar change: paper 2 90/102 to 93/102, where the broken scorer had said 89 to 93

history.note: Observed as a contradiction between two measurements of the same thing, then reproduced deliberately by comparing a file with itself.

Repaired and controlled. The quoted historical figures are NOT corrected: they were measured with the defect and the honest thing is to say so rather than to restate them from a re-run nobody has reviewed.

The stated repair is supported. Live-source inspection confirmed that candidate and baseline both call apply_variants, with the existing-gold-match guard, and the variant-bearing self-comparison control passed. The reviewer is explicit about two limits: this does not validate the historical improvement figures, and it is not frozen-component approval of gold_runner.py, which is not in any review target.

No change. The reviewer: 'No new contrary evidence established here. Their prior assessments retain their stated limits; this review adds no fresh execution verification.' The cycle 01 assessment and its two limits stand as written.

SELF-F04.description: The loop-state controller has a --json flag whose purpose is to give a caller the governing boundary and the section 6 sets without parsing prose, so that no second component has to restate the rule. When every cycle in a run fails the MC-2 gate, the controller takes an early return six hundred lines above the --json branch: it prints a paragraph of English and exits 0. A caller that asked for machine output receives unparseable text under a success code. The flag's own documentation promises it 'exits non-zero exactly as the ordinary run does', and it does, which is the problem: the ordinary run's exit 0 is a human-readable CONTINUE, and through this interface the same 0 asserts that a state was established when none was computed.
SELF-F04.discovery_source: Raised by the BOOTSTRAP-003 cycle 03 reviewer, outside the finding format and therefore not captured in the ledger. Their words: 'loop_state.py:592 returns prose with exit 0 when every cycle is invalid, even with --json. The package rejects that unreadable result, so this path does not recreate SELF-F01's false clean package. It should nevertheless return a defined JSON result or an explicit failure.' Recorded here rather than left in the review body, because a defect that carries no identifier is one nothing in this repository will ask about again.
SELF-F04.affected_component: scripts/loop_state.py, a covered component of the BOOTSTRAP-003 target. The --json branch itself was added on 8 October 2026 as the third repair of SELF-F01.
SELF-F04.severity: Moderate, and lower than it looks. The one caller that exists, approval_package.py, refuses a result it cannot parse, so this does not reach an approval document today. What it is, is a success code asserting something the program never computed, in the interface built specifically so that callers would not have to guess. The next caller written against it will have no reason to expect prose.
SELF-F04.proposed_repair: The early return now honours --json, and the object it emits omits the open, resolved and disputed keys rather than sending them empty. An empty list is the same silent zero this layer keeps finding in itself: a caller cannot tell 'nothing is open' from 'the sets were never computed'. A sets_established field says which it is, and the ordinary branch carries the same field set true, so a caller asks one question instead of inferring from which keys happen to be present. The exit code stays 0, because 'no valid cycle exists' is an answer rather than a failure, and the flag's documented promise about exit codes is kept. Writing the controls for this then exposed a second defect in the same seam, which is repaired here too: approval_package.py reconciles each frozen cycle's own record before it ever consults the controller, and a cycle whose record cannot be read made CannotCalculate escape as a Python traceback. The operator was shown a line number where a stated reason belongs. It now refuses with FINDINGS_STATE: CANNOT_ESTABLISH and quotes the controller.
evidence: scripts/loop_state.py: the --json branch inside the `if not valid:` return, with no set keys and sets_established false, and the same field set true on the ordinary branch
scripts/approval_package.py: the sets_established guard, and the try/except around authoritative_items that turns a controller refusal into a stated refusal

scripts/test_approval_package.py: '--json on a review with no valid cycle: JSON, no sets, and an explicit statement that none were established', 'refused, not crashed: a frozen cycle whose record cannot be read produces a stated reason', and the positive 'a review with valid cycles still reports its sets and says it established them', without which removing the flag entirely would leave the first two green
_probe/mutate_repairs.py: SELF-F04, SELF-F04b and SELF-F04c, one per claim the repair makes

The sets_established guard in the package is deliberately NOT controlled, and the test file says why: nothing today can reach it, because a run with no valid cycle is refused earlier and a run with one always establishes sets. A control there would pass whether or not the guard existed

history.note: Raised as an additional interface issue alongside the cycle's one finding. Disclosed here under the ruling of 5 October: a known defect does not sit outside controlled state tracking merely because no identifier was minted for it.

Repaired and controlled, under Alex Zamurko's instruction of 8 October to repair and test D02-F01 and SELF-F04. Two things are worth recording about how it went rather than only that it went. The flag had no control of any kind before today: it was added yesterday as SELF-F01's third repair and the only thing exercising it was the package's own suite, indirectly, which is why the reviewer found this by reading source instead of by anything going red. And the first fixture written for it was wrong twice over, each time refusing for a reason unrelated to what it claimed to test: it omitted bootstrap_review, so the controller refused on run identity under C01-F05, and it assumed the package would reach the controller at all, when in fact the package reconciles each cycle's own record first. Chasing the second of those is what exposed the traceback defect repaired alongside this one.
